question: The $x$-$t$ graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at $t = 2$ s is :
diagram_alt: Sine curve of x against t with amplitude 1 m, maximum at t = 2 s, zero at 4 s and period 8 s
solution:
From the graph: amplitude $A = 1$ m and period $T = 8$ s, so $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ rad/s and $x = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)$.

At $t = 2$ s, $x = 1$ m (the positive extreme).

$$a = -\omega^2x = -\frac{\pi^2}{16} \times 1 = -\frac{\pi^2}{16}\ \text{m s}^{-2}$$
